s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
Peripapillary hemorrhages and retinal vessel narrowing
key_facts: Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history
Developed ocular symptoms on day 2 post-admission
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Normal complete blood cell counts
Normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with normal results
Fluorescein Angiography showed mild leakage and fluorescein leakage from retinal venules

raw.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
Peripapillary hemorrhages and retinal vessel narrowing
key_facts: Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history
Developed ocular symptoms on day 2 post-admission
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Normal complete blood cell counts
Normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with normal results
Fluorescein Angiography showed mild leakage and fluorescein leakage from retinal venules

raw.rationale: The patient developed ocular symptoms including blurred vision, redness, and pain, with findings of central scotoma, impaired color and contrast vision, and mild anterior chamber inflammation, which are consistent with uveitis. The presence of central nongranulomatous retrodescemetic precipitates and mild vitreous inflammation further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: relative afferent pupillary defect
rejected.why: This is a symptom rather than a diagnosis

rejected.label: pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient was hospitalized for pneumonia, the ocular symptoms are not directly related to pneumonia

rejected.label: hypertension
rejected.why: There is no mention of hypertension in the patient's medical history or laboratory results

rejected.label: lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no evidence to suggest lymphoma, such as abnormal complete blood cell counts or other systemic symptoms
